nodes.title: Powers of a weighted adjacency matrix sum the weights of walks

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the Andrásfai graph is the Cayley graph of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/(3k+2)\mathbb{Z}$ whose connection set $C$ consists of the residues whose representative in $\{0, 1, \dots, 3k+1\}$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $3$: two distinct residues $x$ and $y$ are adjacent when $y - x \in C$ or $x - y \in C$.
nodes.title: Andrásfai graph

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the complete graph on $n$ vertices has exactly $n^{n-2}$ spanning trees.
nodes.title: Cayley's formula

nodes.summary: The Coxeter graph is the simple graph whose $28$ vertices are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ and $j \in \mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$, and whose edges are the following: for each $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, the vertices $(i, j)$ and $(i, j')$ are adjacent when $j - j' = i$ or $j' - j = i$ in $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$, and for each $j$ the vertex $(0, j)$ is adjacent to $(1, j)$, $(2, j)$ and $(3, j)$. nodes.title: Coxeter graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with a binary operation written as multiplication, and let $C \subseteq G$. The *Cayley digraph* $X(G, C)$ is the directed graph whose vertices are the elements of $G$, with an arc $u \to v$ exactly when $v = uc$ for some $c \in C$.
nodes.title: Cayley digraph

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a set of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$, typically a set of transpositions in the symmetric group $S_n$. The edge-transposition graph of $T$ is the simple graph with vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which two distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent if and only if the transposition swapping $i$ and $j$ belongs to $T$.
nodes.title: Edge-transposition graph

nodes.summary: Every finite group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a finite simple graph.
nodes.title: Frucht's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $d$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is a Moore graph of diameter $d$ when $G$ has diameter $d$ and girth $2d + 1$.
nodes.title: Moore graph

nodes.summary: The Petersen graph is the generalized Johnson graph $J(5,2,0)$: its vertices are the $2$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$, and two of them are adjacent exactly when they are disjoint.
nodes.title: Petersen graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
